Subject and basis: I read the source, rubric, candidate, specification, both designs, both tests, the plan and assessment/consumer-context.md myself. All 11 current SHA-256 digests match the declared basis. The candidate generated/hello-world.mjs has digest fe8f4080... and the rubric has digest 028073e4.... The consumer context is present. It says it is assessment-only and claims no pass, and I did not use it as an oracle.

Rubric criteria:
(1) Required artifacts: all 7 are present. test-execution-result.json is correctly absent: the witness contract replaces it with admitted execution evidence, and the rubric does not list it.
(2) Conformance: the spec's content is real. It declares a minimal Node CLI with source surface generated/hello-world.mjs, exact stdout "Hello, world!\n", exit 0 and no install. It lists the design, test and plan assets and says it is not a record of execution.
(3) Implementation design: it defines generated/hello-world.mjs as the sole entry, printing exactly "Hello, world!" plus one newline and exiting 0. It names test/component/hello-cli.test.mjs and test/uat/hello-cli.uat.test.mjs, both of which run the real CLI in a child process and check status and stdout. It matches the spec but does not cite it by path; I don't consider that material.
(4) Source: the file is console.log("Hello, world!"). It has no imports and needs no packages.
(5) Test design: it specifies component and UAT tests that both spawn the real entry with process.execPath and spawnSync from the project root, and assert status 0 and exact stdout. It requires at least 2 passes and 0 failures.
(6) and (7) Test bodies: both files import node:test, node:assert/strict and spawnSync from node:child_process. Both call spawnSync(process.execPath, ['generated/hello-world.mjs']) with the inherited cwd, which is the project root under the declared command. Both assert strictly that status is 0 and stdout is exactly 'Hello, world!\n'. Neither uses a substitute or fixture, so a wrong output or exit code would fail them.
(8) Plan: command is node; args are ["--test","test/component/hello-cli.test.mjs","test/uat/hello-cli.uat.test.mjs"]; expectedTestPassCount is 2; expectedStdoutMatch is "fail 0", which pins no pass count; assertedReturnValue is "Hello, world!".

Execution-result meaning, from the admitted observations of result b425dc00..., which I kept attributed to actor-invocation 8f685f51... and c-call 76c4c1da...:
- Command 0 (node generated/hello-world.mjs, cwd .) exited 0 with no signal or timeout. Stdout was exactly 14 bytes, "Hello, world!\n", digest d9014c46..., and stderr was empty.
- Command 1 (the declared plan command) exited 0 with empty stderr. Stdout showed both named tests passing: tests 2, pass 2, fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 0.
- So the plan command exited 0, the observed pass count (2) meets expectedTestPassCount (2), the "fail 0" text is present, and the direct CLI output equals the asserted return value plus the newline. The plan is satisfied. The rubric's case (no arguments, that stdout, exit 0) and minimumTestPasses of 2 are both met.

Corroboration: in the current workspace I re-ran both commands read-only on Node v24.7.0, with output going only to pipes and /dev/null. The results matched: CLI exit 0, 14 bytes with the same digest d9014c46..., 0 stderr bytes; tests exit 0 with pass 2, fail 0 and 0 stderr bytes. This re-run is supporting evidence only and does not replace the admitted result or its attribution.

Residual notes, none of which changes an outcome:
- The admitted observation has no predicate observations, so I derived plan satisfaction from its raw exit status and output streams.
- The admitted commands ran in a platform sandbox copy whose bytes I did not read, because it is outside my readable scope. Current workspace bytes match the basis, and my current runs reproduce the admitted streams.

Disclosures: I edited no worksite files. A find listing showed file names under the platform's .ai-workspace archive, but I did not read their contents. The node processes I ran wrote no worksite files that I observed, but I cannot rule out runtime or cache writes outside the checked scope. This assessment grants no admission, acceptance or continuation; closure remains with the parent.
